Study:
Attia et al., 2019
Circ Arrhythm Electrophysiol
Population / dataset: Mayo Clinic; 774,783 unique adults. Development: 499,727; independent holdout: 275,056.
Model / representation: 1D CNN with temporal convolutional blocks followed by spatial fusion across leads
Validation design: Patient-level internal validation and large independent holdout test
Interpretability / biological analysis: Limited direct XAI; conventional ECG-feature model showed no single feature approached CNN performance; accuracy was higher in younger adults.
Key distinction / limitation: Foundational large-scale AI-ECG sex-classification study; no external institutional validation.

Study:
Strodthoff et al., 2021
IEEE J Biomed Health Inform
Validation design: Predefined PTB-XL folds; internal held-out test fold
Reported sex-classification performance: Best overall AUROC 0.928 (ensemble); best accuracy 0.849 (xResNet1D101); healthy subgroup AUROC up to 0.962
Interpretability / biological analysis: Benchmarking, uncertainty and exploratory interpretability analyses
Key distinction / limitation: Open reproducible benchmark; in-domain validation only for sex prediction.

Validation design: Development in GESUS with replication in Inter99
Interpretability / biological analysis: ECGradCAM localized strongest sex information to the QRS complex, especially the R-wave downslope; post-hoc logistic model examined QRS/amplitude/timing features.
Key distinction / limitation: Early dedicated explainable sex-classification study; smaller population cohorts than contemporary clinical datasets.

Study:
Lyle et al., 2021
Front Cardiovasc Med
Population / dataset: PhysioNet; Dataset 2 n=8,903 and independent Dataset 1 n=104
Model / representation: Symmetric Projection Attractor Reconstruction (SPAR) + stacked ML
Validation design: Cross-validation in n=8,903; unseen test in n=104
Reported sex-classification performance: Cross-validation: AUROC 0.93, accuracy 86.3%; unseen test: AUROC 0.97, accuracy 91.3%
Interpretability / biological analysis: SPAR directly visualized morphology; mid-precordial leads performed best individually; classification declined at older ages.
Key distinction / limitation: Morphology-focused interpretable ML; unseen external test was small (n=104).

Study:
Siegersma et al., 2022
Eur Heart J Digit Health
Population / dataset: DNN trained on 131,673 normal ECGs; internal validation n=68,500; two external cohorts n=3,303 and n=4,457
Validation design: Large internal validation plus two external cohorts
Reported sex-classification performance: Internal AUROC 0.96; external AUROCs 0.89 and 0.94; internal accuracy 0.89
Interpretability / biological analysis: Sex misclassification associated with ~1.4-fold higher mortality; mediation implicated ventricular rate, QRS duration and ST/T-wave features.
Key distinction / limitation: Strong biological/outcome validation; training restricted to normal ECGs.

Study:
Cabra Lopez et al., 2022
Applied Sciences
ECG input: Derived pseudo-orthogonal X/Y/Z bipolar signals from Holter ECG
Model / representation: Time-frequency RGB representation of XYZ signals + GoogLeNet
Validation design: Repeated/split evaluation within a small authentication-oriented cohort
Interpretability / biological analysis: Compared contributions of X, Y, Z and combined XYZ representations
Key distinction / limitation: Spatial XYZ representation is relevant methodologically, but cohort was small and task was soft-biometric authentication rather than clinical 12-lead generalization.

Study:
Ryu et al., 2023
J Clin Med
ECG input: Standard 12-lead ECG; also evaluated a 1-lead model
Interpretability / biological analysis: Lead-count comparison demonstrated substantial information gain from 12 leads
Key distinction / limitation: Large single-center cohort; no external validation for sex classification.

Population / dataset: Ghent University Hospital; 269,979 ECGs from 82,477 patients; external PTB-XL validation
ECG input: Standard 12-lead ECG; 5-s sliding windows vs full 10-s input
Model / representation: Two CNNs; repeated sliding-window predictions used to estimate prediction certainty
Reported sex-classification performance: Internal AUROC 0.946 (5-s sliding-window model) vs 0.916 (10-s model); external validation preserved performance/certainty pattern
Interpretability / biological analysis: Focus on uncertainty/certainty rather than waveform physiology
Key distinction / limitation: Explicit uncertainty estimation and external validation; exact external sex AUROC not reported in the abstract.

Study:
O’Sullivan et al., 2024
npj Digital Medicine
Population / dataset: Mayo Clinic pediatric cohort; 90,133 unique patients aged ≤18 years
Model / representation: De novo pediatric CNN and transfer learning from an adult-derived AI-ECG
Validation design: 80/10/10 patient split; prespecified pre-, peri- and post-pubertal analyses
Reported sex-classification performance: De novo model: overall AUROC 0.91, accuracy 81%; pre-/peri-/post-pubertal AUROC 0.67/0.91/0.98
Interpretability / biological analysis: Demonstrated strong puberty-linked emergence of ECG sex signal
Key distinction / limitation: Pediatric developmental focus; single-center primary study.

Study:
Sau et al., 2025
Lancet Digital Health
Population / dataset: BIDMC derivation: 1,163,401 ECGs; external UK Biobank: 42,386 ECGs
Model / representation: CNN producing continuous AI-ECG sex probability / sex-discordance score
Validation design: Large internal test plus independent UK Biobank external validation
Interpretability / biological analysis: Sex-discordance score associated with cardiovascular mortality, incident HF/MI and cardiac/body-composition phenotypes, particularly in females.
Key distinction / limitation: Strong external and prognostic validation; primary aim was risk continuum rather than mechanistic waveform/spatial attribution.

Study:
O’Sullivan et al., 2026
npj Digital Medicine
Population / dataset: Texas Children’s Hospital: 118,003 ECGs from 67,578 patients; Boston Children’s: 437,350 training ECGs and 145,784 test ECGs
ECG input: Pediatric standard 12-lead ECGs; 500 Hz (TCH/Mayo) and 250 Hz (BCH)
Model / representation: External validation of Mayo pediatric/adult-derived CNNs; independent BCH residual CNN
Validation design: Multicenter pediatric external validation and independent model replication
Reported sex-classification performance: TCH de novo Mayo model: overall AUROC 0.80; pre-/peri-/post-pubertal 0.64/0.84/0.94. Adult-derived model: 0.79 overall and 0.62/0.82/0.95 by stage.
Interpretability / biological analysis: Saliency/median-waveform analyses emphasized QRS and T waves, particularly precordial leads; replicated pubertal gradient.
Key distinction / limitation: Strong multicenter pediatric confirmation; performance is development-stage dependent and not directly comparable with adult cohorts.

Population / dataset: 324,243 adults across MIMIC-IV (155,626), WCMC/NYP (106,868), PTB-XL (18,752) and Chapman/Ningbo (42,997); one ECG per participant
ECG input: Standard 12-lead ECG with waveform pathway plus reconstructed 3D VCG geometry
Model / representation: Transferred ResNet1D + explicit 13-channel VCG geometry encoder with gated residual fusion
Validation design: MIMIC-IV pretraining → WCMC/NYP fine-tuning/locked test; zero-shot PTB-XL and Chapman/Ningbo; separate PTB-XL data-efficiency analysis
Reported sex-classification performance: WCMC/NYP AUROC 0.954 (95% CI 0.952–0.957), accuracy 0.881; zero-shot PTB-XL AUROC 0.927; Chapman/Ningbo AUROC 0.916
Interpretability / biological analysis: Lead ablation, VCG component ablation and corrected decomposed Integrated Gradients; spatial direction/XYZ/trajectory features; six-group age analyses; conventional ECG comparisons.
Key distinction / limitation: Combines explicit 3D geometry, cross-cohort transfer, two zero-shot external cohorts, data-efficiency testing and multi-level interpretability; retrospective clinical cohorts.
